test_set_price_after_read.py.rationale: Change B lets the admin editor change a price through Catalog.set_price, and the new price must be what the catalog reports afterwards. Change A caches every price the Catalog reads, and B's own test never reads a price before setting it. After the merge, a price read before set_price stays cached, so price() keeps returning the old value. These tests fail on base and on A (no set_price), pass on B, and fail on the merge.

test_price_cache_with_updates.py.rationale: Change A promises that repeated price lookups do not keep hitting the slow backend. A correct merge with B's set_price may re-read the backend once after an update, but it must not drop caching. The first test checks one backend read per SKU. The second checks that, when set_price exists, at most one extra backend read happens across repeated lookups after an update. On A, set_price is absent and that part is skipped.

test_catalog_write_visibility.py.rationale: On every tree, a write made through the Catalog must be visible through the same Catalog. A rejected write must leave the price unchanged. Both tests are guarded on set_price existing, so they pass trivially on base and on A, and they pass on B. On the merge, the stale cache entry from A hides B's update, which breaks update visibility.
